title: Starter set: Reading and Writing
description: Ten questions across all four Reading and Writing domains.

questions.passage: The documentary's director chose a ______ approach to the story, letting long interviews with farmers speak for themselves instead of adding her own commentary or dramatic music.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
choices: restrained
sensational
exhaustive
hostile
questions.explanation: The director holds back: no commentary, no dramatic music. That is a **restrained** approach. *Sensational* is the opposite, and nothing suggests *exhaustive* or *hostile*.

questions.passage: Although critics first dismissed the novel as a minor work, its reputation has grown so much that scholars now consider it ______ to understanding the author's later writing.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
choices: peripheral
essential
harmful
similar
questions.explanation: "Although" sets up a contrast with "minor work," and the reputation "has grown." So the novel is now seen as important: **essential**. *Peripheral* means unimportant, which repeats the old view.

questions.passage: The axolotl, a salamander native to lakes near Mexico City, can regrow lost limbs, parts of its heart, and even portions of its brain. Researchers study the axolotl not because they expect humans to regrow limbs anytime soon, but because identifying the genes that control its regeneration could help improve treatments for wounds and scarring.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices: To explain why researchers are interested in a particular animal's abilities
To argue that humans will soon be able to regrow lost limbs
To describe the lakes where axolotls live
To compare axolotls with other species of salamander
questions.explanation: The text names the axolotl's ability, then explains why scientists study it. B is directly contradicted ("not because they expect humans to regrow limbs").

questions.passage: Malika had practiced the piano piece for months, but when she sat down in front of the audience, her hands felt as if they belonged to someone else. Then she noticed her grandmother in the second row, nodding slowly in time to music that had not started yet. Malika took a breath, placed her fingers on the keys, and began to play along with that silent rhythm.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: A performer overcomes her nerves by drawing on the calm support of a family member.
A performer decides she no longer wants to play the piano.
An audience member criticizes a performance.
A performer forgets the music and leaves the stage.
questions.explanation: Malika starts nervous, sees her grandmother keeping a calm rhythm, and then begins to play. The passage is about getting past nerves with that support.

questions.passage: A student surveyed classmates about their daily screen time and how much they usually sleep. She claims that students who reported more screen time tended to report less sleep.

table.title: Average reported sleep by daily screen time
head: Daily screen time
Average sleep (hours)

questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the student's claim?
choices: Students with less than 2 hours of daily screen time reported an average of 8.1 hours of sleep, while those with more than 6 hours reported an average of 6.4 hours.
Students with 2 to 4 hours of daily screen time reported an average of 7.6 hours of sleep.
Some students reported more than 6 hours of screen time per day.
The average sleep reported by students with 4 to 6 hours of screen time was 7.0 hours.
questions.explanation: The claim is a comparison: more screen time goes with less sleep. Only A compares groups, showing the lowest screen-time group sleeping 1.7 hours more than the highest. B and D each describe a single group.

questions.passage: Some plants in the Kyzylkum Desert, such as the saxaul, have very deep roots that can reach groundwater many meters below the surface. Other desert plants instead spread shallow roots over a wide area to collect water from brief rains before it evaporates. A plant with shallow, widespread roots would therefore most likely ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: be able to absorb water quickly after a rainfall.
depend mainly on groundwater far below the surface.
grow only in places where it never rains.
have roots that reach deeper than those of the saxaul.
questions.explanation: Shallow, wide roots exist to catch rain "before it evaporates," so these plants must take up water quickly after rain. B and D describe the deep-rooted strategy instead.

questions.passage: The three madrasahs of Samarkand's Registan were built over more than two ______ the Ulugbek Madrasah was finished around 1420, and the other two were added in the 1600s.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: centuries:
centuries,
centuries
centuries, which
questions.explanation: The second part is a complete sentence that explains the first, so a colon works. A comma alone is a comma splice, no punctuation is a run-on, and "which" breaks the grammar of the second part.

questions.passage: By the time the researchers published their findings in 2021, they ______ the glacier's movement for nearly a decade.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: track
are tracking
had been tracking
will track
questions.explanation: "By the time" plus a past event (published in 2021) signals an action that continued up to that past point. That calls for the past perfect progressive: **had been tracking**.

questions.passage: Sourdough bread rises because of wild yeast and bacteria living in a fermented starter. Commercial bread, ______ usually relies on a single strain of yeast that is added in a measured amount.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices: by contrast,
for instance,
as a result,
in addition,
questions.explanation: The sentences compare two different ways bread rises, so the second needs a contrast: **by contrast**.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The Pamir Highway runs through Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan.
• It is one of the highest international roads in the world.
• Its highest point, the Ak-Baital Pass, is about 4,655 meters above sea level.
• The road was built in the 1930s.
questions.prompt: The student wants to emphasize the highway's extreme elevation. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The Pamir Highway's highest point, the Ak-Baital Pass, sits about 4,655 meters above sea level.
The Pamir Highway runs through Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan.
The Pamir Highway was built in the 1930s.
The Pamir Highway connects two countries and was built in the 1930s.
questions.explanation: Elevation is the goal, and only A gives a height. The other choices are about location and history.
